chunks: Though you cannot desire except as God will, the Lord of all the worlds.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'What you will, except as God wills' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to illustrate the harmony between divine decree (jabr) and human free will (ikhtiyar), suggesting that human volition is not independent but operates within the scope of Allah's overarching will. It underscores the concept of 'amr bayn al-amrayn' (the matter between the two matters), where humans are empowered to choose yet remain dependent on the Creator's sustaining will. This reinforces the theological principle that all human actions, though acquired, are ultimately created by God.
